A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present the first deterministic algorithms for rectangle enclosure and dominance reporting that run in time proportional to the output size, and we do so in the standard word-RAM model with word size Θ(logn).
we give the first deterministic algorithm for rectangle enclosure that runs in worst-case linear time.
we present the first deterministic algorithms with O(nlogn+k) time for the rectangle enclosure problem, the rectangle dominance reporting problem and the rectangle stabbing query problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can derandomize algorithms for geometric problems in the word-RAMS, even if they use randomness in a non-trivial way.

we show how to derandomize the algorithm of Chan et al. using a new technique that is based on an efficient deterministic variant of the classical randomized technique called “randomized incremental construction”.

derandomization is possible even for randomized algorithms with a non-negligible failure probability, provided that the algorithm is carefully designed to allow efficient failure detection and recovery.
